answer: A staking bond that vests slowly makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after a long delta of honest work, so an attacker who wants to forge a thousand accounts must fund a thousand bonds and wait out the same delay on each. Add a per-identity cipher challenge tied to the bond's public key, so one machine cannot replay a single proof across clones. The cost of a Sybil army then grows linearly with its size, while an honest agent pays only once.
